routing_warnings.description: The question concerns Title and Heading 1 typography rather than deployment of the style catalog.
The client changes the Title font size, which belongs to named-style typography.
The reported break after the third bullet is clarified as Tab-based hierarchy behavior rather than general style deployment.
The client specifically confirms that the list broke when using the Tab key without changing styles.
The Master-template feedback about incorrect bullet sizes and spacing concerns bullet visual design.
The Master-template table and duplicated-text failures concern table interaction stability, not style-system deployment.
The proposal to use Danish style names concerns the language of template interface text and does not establish or replace the separate PBU-prefix convention.
The numbered-list alignment failure at item 10 belongs to the numbered-list formatting Requirement.
The list breaking after the third bullet concerns list hierarchy behavior rather than named-style typography.
The missing green level-four bullet belongs to the bullet visual-design Requirement.
The missing theme colors belong to the controlled theme-color palette Requirement.
The report that the caption style was missing concerns style availability and deployment; the caption typography specification is represented under the target Requirement.
The customer's report that Master-template bullet sizes and spacing remain incorrect concerns bullet visual design.
This message specifies bullet-list visual design across templates rather than Tab-based hierarchy behavior.
The numbered-list alignment failure at item 10 belongs to numbered-list formatting rather than Tab-based hierarchy.
The Master-template feedback concerns bullet sizes and spacing, not the Tab-based hierarchy interaction.
The reported break after the third bullet is tied by messages 65, 67, and 72 to using Tab instead of the style ribbon, making list hierarchy behavior the better target.
The message concerns whether users create list levels with Tab or selected ribbon styles rather than specifying or evaluating bullet glyph appearance.
The statement about Enter adding a new number concerns the Board Meeting row-entry workflow rather than general numbered-list formatting.
This message concerns the visible language of a field label rather than Word's default language configuration.
This message supplies Danish date-placeholder wording rather than changing Word's default language configuration.
This message supplies Danish subject-placeholder wording rather than changing Word's default language configuration.
This message sets the templates' underlying default Word language rather than visible interface wording.
The requirement that fields be unique and not duplicate content concerns field-state independence rather than Danish wording.
This message defines the persistent help-label behavior and label-to-field-text mapping rather than changing the language.
The message specifically concerns a pasted table moving to the right rather than the general legacy-content transfer workflow.
The request to shorten spacing so the content fits on one page belongs to the page-fit spacing Requirement; only the old-to-new copy result belongs to the target Requirement.
The request to omit the footer page number on the first page belongs to the page-number-start Requirement.
The client verifies general old-to-new copy-paste behavior but does not specifically identify pasted-table or column containment.
The right-hand-column displacement is attributed to text fields failing to wrap, not to externally pasted table layouts.
The reported nonworking Master-template tables concern reusable table-element interaction rather than pasted-table containment.
The reported hard-return spacing and multiline behavior concern text entry inside interactive fields, not line breaks following pasted legacy content.
The inability to use Enter in a right-side text area concerns interactive-field multiline entry.
This partial runtime result concerns Enter behavior across interactive text fields rather than post-paste line breaks.
The freelancer's claim that Enter now works everywhere targets interactive-field multiline entry rather than post-paste line breaks.
The reported incorrect bullet sizes and spacing are a concrete bullet-design issue rather than direct evidence of general cross-user rendering inconsistency.
The freelancer's hypothesis concerns use of Tab versus named styles for bullet hierarchy and does not establish a cross-user rendering Event.
The duplicated-text observation concerns independent field content rather than table interaction stability.
The content-checkbox resizing limitation concerns the checklist control itself and does not establish a fix or verification for overall Master-table stability.
The top and bottom spacing claim is narrower field or cell-padding evidence and does not verify overall Master-table stability.
The reported field behavior concerns placeholder clearing rather than the underlying field representation.
The client's preference for grey fields concerns visual identification of editable areas.
This acceptance directly retains dropdown and checklist controls as specialized interactions.
The uniqueness and non-duplication requirement concerns independent field content.
The inconsistent click-and-type behavior concerns direct placeholder replacement.
The request to make a label Danish changes interface-text localization rather than the help-label mechanism.
The requirement that fields be unique and not duplicate content concerns independent field content.
The request to remove placeholder text when a field is activated concerns replacement interaction.
The concern that an empty field will not be visible concerns visual discoverability; the duplicated help text was already established for the target Requirement.
The question asks whether field text is removed on activation.
The reported three-dot typing behavior is execution evidence for placeholder replacement.
The client accepts the preceding proposal about replacing ordinary content controls with simple editable text while retaining specialized controls; this primarily changes field architecture.
This message defines the wording and persistent hover purpose of field labels rather than visual field discoverability.
This message requests direct placeholder replacement when a field is activated rather than a visual identification behavior.
The separate statement that the Master-template tables are not working belongs to the table-interaction stability Requirement.
The request for a Danish field label changes localized interface text rather than date-selection behavior.
The requirement that fields be unique and not duplicate content belongs to field-content independence.
The supplied Danish date-placeholder wording is localized interface text rather than a change to the date-picker mechanism.
The Enter-key result in the first clause concerns multiline field entry; only the spacing clause supports the target Requirement.
The claim that Enter works everywhere concerns multiline field entry, not right-side field padding.
The claim that the margin will not collapse concerns fixed content margins; the stated top-and-bottom spacing does not establish the requested right-side padding.
The excessive spacing described here concerns hard returns inside text-entry fields rather than overall page-fit spacing.
The requested spacing between entered text and the right-hand line is local field-cell padding.
The claimed 0.06 row-and-column spacing implements local table or field padding, not overall page-fit spacing.
The report that spacing is still absent follows the local field-padding change rather than the one-page-fit requirement.
The top-and-bottom spacing claim concerns local field or table spacing; the same message separately addresses multiline entry and fixed margins.
The requested spacing between entered text and the line on the right concerns local field padding rather than fixed outer margins and icon containment.
The claimed 0.06 spacing for rows and columns addresses field or cell padding rather than the target fixed-margin behavior.
This message concerns the extra line or border created when adding a row after a Topic, not static field alignment.
This message establishes the accepted insert-row and field-copy workflow rather than changing field alignment.
The statement that pressing Enter creates a new numbered item concerns automatic numbering behavior, which the target boundary explicitly excludes.
This message concerns alignment of Item and Title with Topic, Proposal, and Start Time rather than agenda-row insertion.
The client specifies the Board Meeting row-insertion workflow rather than requesting or confirming delivery of the Master-table walkthrough.
The message reports malfunctioning Master-template tables and duplicated text, which is runtime evidence for table interaction stability rather than the guidance deliverable.
The freelancer reports a table-style limitation and manual handling method, but does not claim delivery of the requested explanation or walkthrough.
The 0.06 row-and-column spacing claim concerns spacing between field content and cell boundaries rather than paragraph spacing after hard returns.
The statement that spacing was still not applied follows the request for spacing between text and the right-hand line.
The target-specific part of this message claims that Enter now works everywhere; its separate top-and-bottom spacing statement does not unambiguously identify multiline paragraph spacing.
